Subject: SIG follow-up: prompt redaction & ephemeral audit package

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the SIG questionnaire. A couple of follow-ups from our side specifically about prompt/log handling and training:

- Short answer: we do not use customer prompt content to improve models by default; training on customer data requires an explicit opt-in and a separate contract.
- Retention: prompt text and unredacted inference logs for standard hosted customers are retained for up to 30 days by default and then purged; ephemeral modes can be configured for 0–24 hours.
- Redaction: we offer both deterministic (PII regex) and ML-based redaction before logs are persisted; redaction artifacts are recorded in an audit entry.

You mentioned wanting a sample package demonstrating the redaction process and an audit slice for SOC reviewers. I can share a sanitized sample and the steps we take to produce it. Attached is a short text file showing a redaction example and a one-page summary of our approach — will follow with an audit excerpt if that looks useful.

Next steps: if you confirm the scope the reviewers want (sample prompts only / sample prompts + model metadata / full audit slice), we’ll prepare a redacted bundle and an access-controlled drive folder.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up: prompt redaction & ephemeral audit package

Jordan / Marissa —

Quick technical confirmations:

- Ephemeral mode: called "ephemeral-session=0h" in our config. When enabled on a deployment lane, the raw prompt and model KV caches are never written to long-term blob storage; logs are streamed to an in-memory pipeline and expired at the end of the session. Operational traces (request id, timestamp, model variant) are retained for 90 days for debugging but do NOT contain prompt text.

- Redaction storage: we only persist a redaction event record (rule_id, hashed redaction fingerprint, timestamp, actor) — hashed fingerprint is HMAC'd with a tenant-scoped key and cannot be reversed to original tokens. No redacted token fragments or original unredacted prompts are persisted when redaction runs in the default pipeline.

- Export package: I exported a small audit slice covering 2027-06-15 to 2027-07-10 and included the redaction event CSV. I also generated 10 sanitized prompt pairs per Sarah’s request and put everything into an access-controlled drive folder. Attachments: audit_log_excerpt.csv, redaction_sample.txt.

I’ll drop a short attestation we can copy into the email: "Redwood Inference attests that prompt text included in the supplied sanitized package will not be used for model training or evaluation except upon explicit written opt-in by MedSys Health. Redacted fragments and original prompt content are not stored persistently when redaction is enabled; audit records include only rule identifiers and hashed fingerprints."

Let me know if you want the HMAC key derivation info or a sample of the hashing code (we can supply).

—Dev

dev.patel@redwood.com

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal export and Dev’s notes above, attached is the sanitized package you requested:

- 10 prompt pairs (original -> redacted) — redaction_sample.txt
- Audit slice (redaction events) — audit_log_excerpt.csv
- Short attestation (copyable) and README — sig_response_summary.pdf

Highlights / answers to your specific questions:
- Default retention: hosted accounts = 30 days for unredacted logs; we can enable ephemeral-session=0h for POC environments to avoid persisting prompt text.
- Redaction artifacts: no redacted token fragments or original prompts are stored when redaction is enabled; only anonymized event records with HMAC'd fingerprints and rule ids are kept.
- Training: Redwood will not use any customer prompts for model training without written opt-in from MedSys. That is our standard commitment and we have included the attestation in the package.
